content: The Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education (ACCME) is the governing body responsible for overseeing continuing medical education (CME) in the United States. The ACCME establishes and enforces standards for the accreditation of all providers of CME activities. The ACCME is composed of seven member organizations: the American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS), the American Hospital Association (AHA), the American Medical Association (AMA), the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC), the Association for Hospital Medical Education (AHME), the Council of Medical Specialty Societies (CMSS), and the Federation of State Medical Boards of the United States, Inc. (FSMB). The mission of the ACCME is to identify, develop, and promote standards for high-quality continuing medical education. These standards are designed to help physicians maintain their professional competence, integrate new medical knowledge, and ultimately improve the quality of care provided to patients and their communities. The ACCME achieves its mission through a voluntary, self-regulated accreditation system for CME providers. This system includes a peer-review process that adapts to changes in medical education and the healthcare delivery system. The primary responsibilities of the ACCME include the following: Acting as the accrediting body for institutions and organizations that provide continuing medical education. Recognizing institutions and organizations that offer accreditation for CME providers. Developing criteria to evaluate educational programs and activities, which are used by the ACCME and state accrediting bodies to accredit institutions and organizations. Recommending and initiating studies aimed at improving the organization and processes of CME and its accreditation.
